Subject: Refurbished CX-10: repeat E34 lockouts and a warranty dispute over scale

We bought this refurbished Vantorre CX-10 (s/n VT21-30877) for $14,800 inc GST, delivered and commissioned 14 September. This is what's happened in the eight weeks since.

22 Sept. Kelsall's tech attended for E34 (steam generator low water level), which was locking us out of combi and steam modes. The error log showed nine E34s since delivery. Water level sensor replaced under warranty. Inlet pressure measured at 320 kPa and recorded as OK.

3 Oct. We reported E34 was back, four times that week, and that the core probe was reading low. Tested twice in a lamb shoulder against a Thermapen: oven 63°C, Thermapen 70°C both times.

6 Oct. Tech found the steam generator heavily scaled, descaled and flushed it, and recalibrated the probe to within 1 degree. The report recommended we install a water softener, saying the scale indicated hard water.

Our water. Our water supplier told us the Fitzroy supply averages about 15 mg/L hardness as CaCO3, which they class as soft. The oven had been on it for 22 days when the scale was found. The listing says the steam generator was descaled before sale. We don't see how heavy scale forms in three weeks on water that soft.

24 Oct. E34 locked the oven out at 6.10pm on a Saturday with 60 covers booked. We finished the lamb on the stove and in the deck oven and pulled the pork belly for the night.

27 Oct. Tech attended for E34 again and found more scale. Kelsall's position is that it's a site water issue and not covered by warranty, and they're invoicing us $280 + GST ($308) for that visit. The unit was six weeks into a six month parts and labour warranty.

The tech has been good to deal with throughout. Our issue is with the unit and the warranty call. If you're looking at a refurbished combi, ask for the descale record and get it in writing how scale is treated under warranty before you pay.
